text:
Carter Verhaeghe opened with a hat trick against Seattle on Oct. 17 and hasn't really stopped: 10 goals and 16 points in 18 games, 8 of those points on the power play. For a three-time Cup winner who was shooting 13% last season, this is a different gear.

It's mostly a gear the puck chose. He's at 27% shooting, with 10 goals on 6.9 expected, and Florida has scored 7.2 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice. Both of those tend to come back to earth. The chances themselves are good, though: 1.24 expected goals per 60, up from 0.94 last season.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking adds the part of his game that doesn't need luck. Last season 72% of his exits left the zone with possession and he was 93rd percentile among forwards in primary shot assists. Our season-end range of 26 to 41 goals says he keeps scoring, just not at this pace. Florida has lost two straight, so the timing of the cool-off matters.
headline: Verhaeghe's shot is falling, for now
